items.followUp: How are the results of a biological investigation communicated to other scientists?

rubric.why: Identifies the form or means used to report results.
rubric.description: Results are written in a research paper and published in a scientific journal.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming a research paper or scientific journal as the means of reporting results.

rubric.why: Shows the purpose of reporting results.
rubric.description: Reporting makes the findings available to other scientists.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that reporting communicates or shares findings with other scientists.

modelAnswer: The results of a biological investigation are written in a research paper.
The paper is published in a scientific journal to communicate the findings to other scientists.

items.followUp: What are grana, and how are they related to thylakoids?

rubric.why: Identifies the structure of a thylakoid.
rubric.description: Thylakoids are flattened, membrane-bound sacs inside chloroplasts.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing thylakoids as flattened or disc-shaped membrane sacs.

rubric.description: Thylakoids are arranged in stacks called grana.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that thylakoids form stacks called grana.

modelAnswer: Thylakoids are flattened, membrane-bound sacs found inside chloroplasts.
They are arranged in stacks called grana.

items.followUp: Give one example each of an autotroph and a heterotroph.

rubric.description: Autotrophs make their own food, usually by photosynthesis.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that autotrophs make their own food or carry out photosynthesis.

rubric.description: Heterotrophs cannot make their own food and depend on other organisms for it.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that heterotrophs obtain food from other organisms or cannot make their own food.

modelAnswer: Autotrophs make their own food, usually by photosynthesis.
Heterotrophs cannot make their own food and obtain it from other organisms.

items.followUp: Write two characteristics of Kingdom Fungi.

rubric.why: Gives a defining cellular characteristic of protists.
rubric.description: Protists are eukaryotic organisms with a true nucleus.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that protists are eukaryotic or have a true nucleus.

rubric.why: Gives a common organisational characteristic of protists.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that most protists are unicellular.

modelAnswer: Protists are eukaryotic organisms with a true nucleus.

items.followUp: What happens to DNA during the S-phase of the cell cycle?

rubric.why: Identifies the main event of S-phase.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that DNA is copied or replicated.

rubric.why: States the outcome of DNA replication.
rubric.description: Each chromosome forms two sister chromatids, and the cell's DNA content doubles.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that sister chromatids form or that DNA content doubles.

modelAnswer: During S-phase, the DNA in the cell is replicated.
Each chromosome forms two sister chromatids, so the cell's DNA content doubles.

items.followUp: What is the G₁ phase of the cell cycle?

rubric.description: G₀ is a resting or quiescent phase outside the active cell cycle.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying G₀ as a resting or quiescent phase.

rubric.why: Explains the cell's state in G₀.
rubric.description: Cells in G₀ have left the active cell cycle and are not dividing.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that cells are outside the active cycle or are not dividing.

modelAnswer: G₀ is a resting or quiescent phase in which a cell leaves the active cell cycle.
The cell is not dividing during this phase, although it may remain metabolically active.

items.followUp: How does binary fission differ from budding?

rubric.why: Identifies the type of reproduction and parent involved.
rubric.description: Binary fission is a form of asexual reproduction involving one parent.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying it as asexual reproduction or stating that it involves one parent.

rubric.why: Describes the defining outcome of binary fission.
rubric.description: The parent cell divides to form two daughter cells.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that one cell divides into two daughter cells.

modelAnswer: Binary fission is a type of asexual reproduction involving one parent.
The parent cell divides to form two daughter cells.

items.followUp: Write the word equation for photosynthesis.

rubric.why: Identifies the food product made during photosynthesis.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming glucose or carbohydrate as a product.

rubric.why: Identifies the other main product of photosynthesis.
rubric.description: Oxygen is released as a product.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming oxygen as a product.

modelAnswer: The main products of photosynthesis are glucose and oxygen.
Glucose is a carbohydrate made by the plant, and oxygen is released.
